newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rightwing killer seeks amnesty - report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rightwing killer seeks amnesty - report.

text.p: Convicted right-wing mass murderer, Barend Strydom, freed from prison in 1992 under a government pardon, has applied to South Africa's "truth commission" for amnesty, state television said on Thursday.

The national broadcaster quoted his lawyer as saying that Strydom, who randomly shot dead seven blacks in 1988 because he said they threatened the survival of the Afrikaner nation, would seek amnesty from prosecution under civil claims.

However, television said a spokesman for the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, set up to uncover human rights abuses during the apartheid years in a bid to clear up and heal the past, could not confirm Strydom's application.

Strydom will be the latest in a line of applicants to seek pardon from the truth body. This follows an announcement last month that former police minister Adriaan Vlok had applied to the body, making him the first member of an apartheid-era cabinet ready to admit to abuses.
